lesson_scope: First-order differential equation modeling with exponential and logarithmic functions, separation of variables, initial value problem solving, and asymptotic analysis.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Direct proportional growth differential equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Direct proportional growth differential equation.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{y}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int 3\,\mathrm{d}x \implies \ln|y| = 3x + c$$

Use the initial condition $x = 0, y = 5$:
$$\ln 5 = 3(0) + c \implies c = \ln 5$$
$$\ln\left(\frac{y}{5}\right) = 3x \implies y = 5\mathrm{e}^{3x}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Half-life evaluation in exponential decay model.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Half-life evaluation in exponential decay model.

walkthrough.text:
Write the exponential decay equation:
$$N(t) = 200\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t}$$

Set $N = 100$ to find the half-life:
$$100 = 200\mathrm{e}^{-0.05t} \implies \mathrm{e}^{-0.05t} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \mathrm{e}^{0.05t} = 2$$
$$0.05t = \ln 2 \implies t = \frac{\ln 2}{1/20} = 20\ln 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Shifted linear differential equation integration.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Shifted linear differential equation integration.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate both sides:
$$\int \frac{1}{y - 10}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int 2\,\mathrm{d}t$$

Integrate to obtain the general logarithmic solution:
$$\ln(y - 10) = 2t + c \implies y - 10 = \mathrm{e}^{2t + c} = A\mathrm{e}^{2t} \implies y = 10 + A\mathrm{e}^{2t}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Separable ODE with power on LHS and decaying exponential on RHS.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separable ODE with power on LHS and decaying exponential on RHS.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int v\,\mathrm{d}v = \int \mathrm{e}^{-2t}\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \frac{1}{2}v^2 = -\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2t} + c$$

Substitute $t = 0, v = 3$ to solve for $c$:
$$\frac{1}{2}(3)^2 = -\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^0 + c \implies \frac{9}{2} = -\frac{1}{2} + c \implies c = 5$$
$$\frac{1}{2}v^2 = 5 - \frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2t} \implies v^2 = 10 - \mathrm{e}^{-2t} \implies v = \sqrt{10 - \mathrm{e}^{-2t}}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separable geometric differential equation.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int y\,\mathrm{d}y = \int x\,\mathrm{d}x \implies \frac{1}{2}y^2 = \frac{1}{2}x^2 + c \implies y^2 = x^2 + 2c$$

Apply initial condition $(x = 0, y = 4)$:
$$4^2 = 0^2 + 2c \implies 2c = 16 \implies y^2 = x^2 + 16$$

Calculate $y$ when $x = 3$:
$$y = \sqrt{3^2 + 16} = \sqrt{9 + 16} = \sqrt{25} = 5$$

ai_rubric.observable: Separates variables $\int y\,\mathrm{d}y = \int x\,\mathrm{d}x \implies y^2 = x^2 + c$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Drill: Rate constant evaluation in cooling model.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rate constant evaluation in cooling model.

walkthrough.text:
Integrate the Newton cooling differential equation:
$$\int \frac{1}{\theta - 15}\,\mathrm{d}\theta = \int -k\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \ln(\theta - 15) = -kt + c$$

Use $\theta(0) = 75$:
$$\ln(75 - 15) = c \implies c = \ln 60 \implies \theta(t) = 15 + 60\mathrm{e}^{-kt}$$

Use $\theta(5) = 45$ to solve for $k$:
$$45 = 15 + 60\mathrm{e}^{-5k} \implies 30 = 60\mathrm{e}^{-5k} \implies \mathrm{e}^{-5k} = \frac{1}{2} \implies \mathrm{e}^{5k} = 2$$
$$5k = \ln 2 \implies k = \frac{1}{5}\ln 2$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Newton cooling differential equation explicit solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Newton cooling differential equation explicit solution.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{T - 20}\,\mathrm{d}T = \int -0.02\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \ln(T - 20) = -0.02t + c$$

Substitute initial condition $t = 0, T = 100$:
$$\ln(100 - 20) = c \implies c = \ln 80$$
$$\ln\left(\frac{T - 20}{80}\right) = -0.02t \implies T(t) = 20 + 80\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exact logarithmic target time evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Set $T = 40$ in the solution formula:
$$40 = 20 + 80\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} \implies 20 = 80\mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} \implies \mathrm{e}^{-0.02t} = \frac{1}{4}$$

Invert both sides and take natural logarithms:
$$\mathrm{e}^{0.02t} = 4 \implies 0.02t = \ln 4$$
$$t = \frac{\ln 4}{0.02} = 50\ln 4$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Exponential rate modifier variable separation proof.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Exponential rate modifier variable separation proof.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{M}\,\mathrm{d}M = -k\int \mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \ln M = -k\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t}}{-0.1}\right) + c = 10k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} + c$$

Apply initial condition $t = 0, M = 50$:
$$\ln 50 = 10k\mathrm{e}^0 + c \implies c = \ln 50 - 10k$$

Substitute $c$ and factorize:
$$\ln M = 10k\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} + \ln 50 - 10k \implies \ln\left(\frac{M}{50}\right) = 10k\left(\mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} - 1\right)$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rate constant and asymptotic mass evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $t = 10$ and $M = 25$ into the equation from part (a):
$$\ln\left(\frac{25}{50}\right) = 10k\left(\mathrm{e}^{-0.1(10)} - 1\right) \implies \ln\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 10k\left(\mathrm{e}^{-1} - 1\right)$$

Solve for $k$ using $\ln(1/2) = -\ln 2$:
$$-\ln 2 = -10k(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-1}) \implies k = \frac{\ln 2}{10(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-1})}$$

Evaluate the limit as $t \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{t \to \infty} \mathrm{e}^{-0.1t} = 0 \implies \ln\left(\frac{M_\infty}{50}\right) = 10k(0 - 1) = -10k$$
$$M_\infty = 50\mathrm{e}^{-10k} = 50\mathrm{e}^{-\frac{\ln 2}{1 - \mathrm{e}^{-1}}}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Rational rate differential equation with power law solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rational rate differential equation with power law solution.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate both sides:
$$\int \frac{1}{m}\,\mathrm{d}m = -2\int \frac{1}{t + 1}\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \ln m = -2\ln(t + 1) + c$$

Rewrite using logarithm power rules:
$$\ln m = \ln\left((t + 1)^{-2}\right) + c \implies m = \mathrm{e}^c (t + 1)^{-2} = \frac{A}{(t + 1)^2}$$

Apply initial condition $t = 0, m = 100$:
$$100 = \frac{A}{(0 + 1)^2} \implies A = 100 \implies m(t) = \frac{100}{(t + 1)^2}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Rate of change calculation at specific time value.

walkthrough.text:
Find the mass $m$ when $t = 3$:
$$m(3) = \frac{100}{(3 + 1)^2} = \frac{100}{16} = \frac{25}{4} \text{ grams}$$

Substitute $t = 3$ and $m = \frac{25}{4}$ into the rate equation:
$$\left|\frac{\mathrm{d}m}{\mathrm{d}t}\right| = \frac{2}{3 + 1}m = \frac{2}{4}\left(\frac{25}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{25}{4}\right) = \frac{25}{8} \text{ g/s}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Separation of variables with decaying exponential RHS.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Separation of variables with decaying exponential RHS.

hints: Integrate LHS to $-\ln(10 - x)$ and RHS to $4\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t}}{-0.5}\right) = -8\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t}$.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{10 - x}\,\mathrm{d}x = 4\int \mathrm{e}^{-0.5t}\,\mathrm{d}t \implies -\ln(10 - x) = 4\left(\frac{\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t}}{-0.5}\right) + c = -8\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t} + c$$

Substitute initial condition $t = 0, x = 2$:
$$-\ln(10 - 2) = -8\mathrm{e}^0 + c \implies -\ln 8 = -8 + c \implies c = 8 - \ln 8$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Explicit solution and logarithmic point evaluation.

walkthrough.text:
Substitute $c = 8 - \ln 8$ into the equation and isolate $x$:
$$-\ln(10 - x) = -8\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t} + 8 - \ln 8 \implies \ln\left(\frac{10 - x}{8}\right) = 8\left(\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t} - 1\right)$$
$$\frac{10 - x}{8} = \mathrm{e}^{8(\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t} - 1)} \implies x(t) = 10 - 8\mathrm{e}^{8(\mathrm{e}^{-0.5t} - 1)}$$

Substitute $t = 2\ln 2$:
$$\mathrm{e}^{-0.5(2\ln 2)} = \mathrm{e}^{-\ln 2} = \frac{1}{2}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Population growth with baseline offset explicit ODE solution.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Population growth with baseline offset explicit ODE solution.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables and integrate:
$$\int \frac{1}{P - 50}\,\mathrm{d}P = \int \frac{1}{20}\,\mathrm{d}t \implies \ln(P - 50) = \frac{t}{20} + c$$

Apply initial condition $t = 0, P = 150$:
$$\ln(150 - 50) = c \implies c = \ln 100$$

Exponentiate to obtain explicit formula:
$$\ln\left(\frac{P - 50}{100}\right) = \frac{t}{20} \implies P - 50 = 100\mathrm{e}^{t/20} \implies P(t) = 50 + 100\mathrm{e}^{t/20}$$

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Population doubling and instant growth rate evaluation.

hints: Use original ODE for rate of growth: $\frac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{450 - 50}{20} = \frac{400}{20} = 20$.

walkthrough.text:
Set $P = 450$ to solve for $t$:
$$450 = 50 + 100\mathrm{e}^{t/20} \implies 400 = 100\mathrm{e}^{t/20} \implies \mathrm{e}^{t/20} = 4$$
$$\frac{t}{20} = \ln 4 = \ln(2^2) = 2\ln 2 \implies t = 40\ln 2$$

Calculate the rate of growth at $P = 450$ directly from the differential equation:
$$\frac{\mathrm{d}P}{\mathrm{d}t} = \frac{450 - 50}{20} = \frac{400}{20} = 20 \text{ individuals/year}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Nonlinear quotient variable separation differential equation.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Nonlinear quotient variable separation differential equation.

walkthrough.text:
Separate variables:
$$\int \frac{y}{y^2 + 1}\,\mathrm{d}y = \int \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\,\mathrm{d}x$$

Integrate both sides:
$$\frac{1}{2}\int \frac{2y}{y^2 + 1}\,\mathrm{d}y = -\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x} + c \implies \frac{1}{2}\ln(y^2 + 1) = -\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^{-2x} + c$$

Substitute $x = 0, y = 0$:
$$\frac{1}{2}\ln(0 + 1) = -\frac{1}{2}\mathrm{e}^0 + c \implies 0 = -\frac{1}{2} + c \implies c = \frac{1}{2}$$
$$\frac{1}{2}\ln(y^2 + 1) = \frac{1}{2}\left(1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}\right) \implies \ln(y^2 + 1) = 1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}$$

ai_rubric.observable: Integrates LHS using derivative-over-function quotient rule: $\frac{1}{2}\ln(y^2 + 1)$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Explicit radical solution and asymptotic limit evaluation.

hints: From $\ln(y^2 + 1) = 1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}$, exponentiate both sides to get $y^2 + 1 = \mathrm{e}^{1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}}$.

walkthrough.text:
Exponentiate both sides of the logarithmic equation:
$$y^2 + 1 = \mathrm{e}^{1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}} \implies y^2 = \mathrm{e}^{1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}} - 1$$
$$y(x) = \sqrt{\mathrm{e}^{1 - \mathrm{e}^{-2x}} - 1}$$

Evaluate the limit as $x \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{x \to \infty} \mathrm{e}^{-2x} = 0 \implies \lim_{x \to \infty} y(x) = \sqrt{\mathrm{e}^{1 - 0} - 1} = \sqrt{\mathrm{e} - 1}$$

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured: Logistic partial fraction separation of variables.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Logistic partial fraction separation of variables.

hints: Multiply through by 100 to establish the result.

walkthrough.text:
Decompose the rational integrand into partial fractions:
$$\frac{1}{N(100 - N)} = \frac{1}{100}\left(\frac{1}{N} + \frac{1}{100 - N}\right)$$

Separate variables and integrate both sides:
$$\frac{1}{100}\int \left(\frac{1}{N} + \frac{1}{100 - N}\right)\,\mathrm{d}N = k\int \mathrm{e}^{-t/10}\,\mathrm{d}t$$
$$\frac{1}{100}\left[\ln N - \ln(100 - N)\right] = -10k\mathrm{e}^{-t/10} + c_1$$

Combine logarithms and multiply by 100:
$$\frac{1}{100}\ln\left(\frac{N}{100 - N}\right) = -10k\mathrm{e}^{-t/10} + c_1 \implies \ln\left(\frac{N}{100 - N}\right) = -1000k\mathrm{e}^{-t/10} + C$$

ai_rubric.observable: Integrates LHS to $\frac{1}{100}\ln\left(\frac{N}{100 - N}\right)$ and RHS to $-10k\mathrm{e}^{-t/10} + c_1$.
Multiplies by 100 to obtain $\ln\left(\frac{N}{100 - N}\right) = -1000k\mathrm{e}^{-t/10} + C$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Double logarithmic initial value parameter estimation and capacity limit deduction.

walkthrough.text:
Use initial condition $t = 0, N = 20$ to express $C$ in terms of $k$:
$$\ln\left(\frac{20}{100 - 20}\right) = -1000k\mathrm{e}^0 + C \implies \ln\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = -1000k + C \implies C = 1000k - \ln 4$$

Substitute $t = 10\ln 2, N = 50$ where $\mathrm{e}^{-(10\ln 2)/10} = \mathrm{e}^{-\ln 2} = \frac{1}{2}$:
$$\ln\left(\frac{50}{50}\right) = -1000k\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + (1000k - \ln 4)$$
$$0 = -500k + 1000k - \ln 4 \implies 500k = \ln 4 \implies k = \frac{\ln 4}{500}$$

Evaluate $C$:
$$C = 1000\left(\frac{\ln 4}{500}\right) - \ln 4 = 2\ln 4 - \ln 4 = \ln 4$$

Find the limiting population as $t \to \infty$:
$$\lim_{t \to \infty} \mathrm{e}^{-t/10} = 0 \implies \ln\left(\frac{N_\infty}{100 - N_\infty}\right) = C = \ln 4$$
$$\frac{N_\infty}{100 - N_\infty} = 4 \implies N_\infty = 400 - 4N_\infty \implies 5N_\infty = 400 \implies N_\infty = 80$$
